svg.title: Глава 6 — Транспортный уровень: итоговая шпаргалка
svg.desc: Вся глава: services → protocol elements → congestion → UDP/RTP → TCP → QUIC/BBR → performance
svg.text: Вся глава: services → protocol elements → congestion → UDP/RTP → TCP → QUIC/BBR → performance

text.tspan: Transport hides network details from applications.
Berkeley flow: SOCKET/BIND/LISTEN/ACCEPT/CONNECT.
SEND/RECEIVE transfer data; CLOSE releases connection.
Socket API может представлять разные transport services.
Process addressing / ports / TSAP.
Connection establishment must reject old duplicates.
Release is nontrivial; timers and state matter.
Multiplexing, flow/error control and crash recovery.
Congestion occurs in network, offered load comes from transport.
Sender must reduce rate when path is overloaded.
AIMD: additive increase + multiplicative decrease.
Goal: efficient and fair sharing of bottleneck capacity.
UDP: ports, multiplexing, checksum; minimal semantics.
No built-in flow/congestion/retransmission mechanisms.
RPC maps network request/response to procedure-style calls.
RTP carries real-time media timing information.
RTCP provides feedback and synchronization.
Reliable ordered byte stream over unreliable internetwork.
Sockets/ports identify endpoints.
Sequence/ACK/timers drive loss recovery.
Receiver window handles flow control.
Connection establishment/release maintains endpoint state.
Congestion window limits sender by network conditions.
Slow start expands from a conservative initial rate.
Duplicate ACK/loss signals trigger recovery.
SACK improves multi-loss recovery; ECN adds explicit signal.
CUBIC grows congestion window as a time-based cubic function.
QUIC operates over UDP and changes connection/stream handling.
Goal includes reducing setup overhead for modern applications.
BBR estimates bottleneck bandwidth and RTT.
Transport evolution also targets semantics TCP sockets lack.
Chapter notes continued development rather than one final design.
Bottleneck can be CPU/processing rather than line capacity.
Reduce copying and context switches.
Fast path optimizes the common successful case.
Timer data structures affect protocol processing cost.
Header compression trades state for fewer transmitted bits.
Bandwidth-delay product = bandwidth × RTT.
Window must be large enough to keep long fast path busy.
Go-Back-N style recovery wastes more at large BDP.
Feedback latency can dominate protocol behavior.
No universal kernel/socket tuning CLI is prescribed.

svg.text: Provenance: RAG p0564:c01–p0684:c01 · detailed visual covers sections 6.1–6.8
